clue.text: Son legally put end to court activity

parts.note: to quash a verdict or ruling is to annul it in law

explanation.surface: A son's legal action brought some activity in the courts to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, matching 'legally', but here it is the walled court where the racket game is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash is a racket sport played in an enclosed court, so it is an activity on a court.

clue.text: Part of 24's issue, having single-handedly taken on follower of Sun

indicators.note: taking on means adding a further piece after the first one

parts.note: doing something single-handedly is doing it solo
Mon, short for Monday, follows Sun, short for Sunday

explanation.surface: Someone did a solo job taking on a devotee of the sun, and that is part of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is DAVID, the biblical king; his issue means his offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon was a son of King David, so he is one of David's children, part of his issue.

clue.text: Like city, one in SA, lacking capital

indicators.note: lacking its capital means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Durban is a city in South Africa, SA

explanation.surface: Something city-like, one of them in South Africa, has no capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective for towns and cities, so it describes what is city-like.

clue.text: This occasion for celebration isn't without appointed date in state

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are placed within the word for state

parts.note: to state is to say
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't
SD abbreviates sine die, Latin for an adjournment without an appointed date

explanation.surface: A festive occasion is not happening, since no date has been set in the state.
explanation.walkthrough: SINE DIE (SD) is a legal phrase used for a meeting adjourned with no date fixed to resume.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's feast day is a religious occasion for celebration, as the themed days in this puzzle are.

clue.text: It's tossed in the air for last-gasp touchdown

definitions.meaning: a flat batter cake flipped in the pan on Shrove Tuesday
a ... landing is an emergency one where an aircraft drops flat onto the ground

explanation.surface: Something thrown skyward for a desperate late score, as in a rugby game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touchdown' suggests a rugby or American football score but means an aircraft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancakes are flipped in the air when cooked, and a pancake landing is a forced flat landing of a plane.

clue.text: Under pressure, a ploy for a snake handler

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming below, so the later pieces follow the first

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a ploy is a trick

explanation.surface: Pressed hard, someone uses a ruse to deal with a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says St Patrick drove the snakes out of Ireland, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Patrick is credited in legend with banishing serpents from Ireland, so he dealt with snakes.

clue.text: Potential bidder in auction, or this

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who might bid at a sale, or this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The auction is the bidding stage of the card game bridge, where the four players are named after compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the player sitting North bids during the auction, so that seat is a potential bidder.

clue.text: Fled back, lacking energy, inside a place for retirement

indicators.note: inside places the shortened word within the word for a place to sleep

parts.note: a bed is where one retires for the night

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken out of the word for back

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone ran off backwards, worn out, into a retirement home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the verb, to support a motion; 'lacking' drops the energy letter, and 'place for retirement' is where one sleeps, not a care home.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to run away secretly, so absconded is a synonym of fled.

clue.text: Complete, or incomplete course, about the writer

indicators.note: about means the shortened course goes around the writer's letter
incomplete means the last letter of the word for course is cut off

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
the writer refers to the setter, I

explanation.surface: A writer considers whether a course is complete or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' trims ENTREE to ENTRE, which goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, with nothing missing, which is what complete means.

clue.text: Annual ceremony in England and in Germany in part of spring

indicators.note: in places the German word within the spring month

parts.note: May is one of the spring months
und is German for and

explanation.surface: A yearly ceremony held in England and Germany in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Maundy Thursday sees the British monarch hand out special Maundy money to pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal Maundy service, held the Thursday before Easter, is a yearly English ceremony.

clue.text: Train club in new way that makes things go more smoothly

definitions.text: that makes things go more smoothly

indicators.note: arranging the letters in a new way signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coaching a club along new lines helps it run more smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil and grease reduce friction between moving parts, easing their motion.

clue.text: Took again in about 24 hrs

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Sat, short for Saturday, is a day of 24 hours

explanation.surface: Someone retook something in roughly a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly' but supplies RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit an exam is to take it again, and resat is its past tense.

clue.text: Producer of pictures, including kind of adult sci-fi movie

parts.note: a man is one kind of adult person
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 science fiction film

explanation.surface: A film studio's output includes a kind of adult science-fiction picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adult' with 'movie' suggests X-rated fare, but MAN is simply one kind of adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French painter, so he produced pictures.

clue.text: With whom one can have close call, hour being out of joint

definitions.text: With whom one can have close call

indicators.note: something out of joint is dislocated, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone who can be phoned at short notice when time has gone haywire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close call' suggests a narrow escape but means a call to someone close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living next door is close enough to call on or chat with over the fence.

clue.text: 4 across, 8, and 14 all do this and I also have one

definitions.text: 4 across, 8, and 14 all do this and I also have one

parts.words: 4 across, 8, and 14 all do this and I also have one
parts.note: Pancake, Maundy and Mothering each come before a day of the week or year, so each labels one; the setter also has a saint's feast day of his own

explanation.surface: Three earlier answers all perform this action, and the setter shares in it too.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is what those entries do: Pancake Day, Maundy Thursday, Mothering Sunday. The setter Brendan has a feast day, St Brendan's, on 16 May.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's feast-day of the saint they are called after is celebrated in many countries like a birthday.

clue.text: Taking care of second cycle

parts.note: mo, as in 'wait a mo', is a moment or second
Wagner's Ring cycle of operas is known as The Ring

explanation.surface: Looking after a second round of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Mothering Sunday is the British name for Mother's Day, one of the theme's days.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to look after them, so mothering means caring for.

clue.text: Works for essentials, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: needs are the essentials one must have

explanation.surface: Factories for basic goods, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun, a factory, but it is the verb, as in working dough.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker kneads dough, working it with the hands, so kneads and works are synonyms here.

clue.text: Some of them end a blemish that's not beyond correcting

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people put an end to a blemish that can still be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct it, so something emendable can still be put right.

clue.text: Didn't go steady, besotted

indicators.note: besotted suggests muddled or intoxicated, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An infatuated lover stopped dating steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go steady' looks like a phrase about dating, but 'steady' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stayed remained where they were rather than leaving.

clue.text: Way to cook ocean fish, initially

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the ocean
fry are young fish, fish at their first stage of life

explanation.surface: How to cook a sea fish, to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but says fry are fish in their early stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-frying, immersing food in hot fat, is a cooking method.

clue.text: Item's aim framed by a mouthpiece

indicators.note: framed by means the aim word is enclosed by the other pieces

parts.note: the gum is a piece of the mouth
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An item aims to be set in a musician's mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouthpiece' suggests part of an instrument, but means a piece of the mouth, the gum.
explanation.definitionFit: An agendum is a single item on an agenda, the Latin singular of the word.

clue.text: Counterpart of 4 down, 24 and 29 again securing academic title

indicators.note: securing means holding the title inside the word for again

parts.note: anew means again
Dr, doctor, is an academic title

explanation.surface: An equal of three other clue entries, again holding a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: The four patron saints of the British Isles are Patrick, David, George and Andrew, of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is Scotland's patron saint, matching Patrick, David and George for Ireland, Wales and England.

clue.text: I'd turned up, clothed by greatest European dressmaker

indicators.note: clothed by means wrapped inside the word for greatest

parts.note: most means greatest in amount

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, I'd without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: I'd arrived, dressed by Europe's finest couturier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ID to DI, which is 'clothed by' MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a fashionable milliner or dressmaker, from the French word.

clue.text: Handy American source of energy moving East to North

parts.note: US abbreviates American, as in US citizens

indicators.note: in a down clue the north is the top, so E for East is moved to the start of the word

parts.note: fuel is what supplies energy

explanation.surface: A practical US energy supply relocates from the east to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving East to North' shifts the E of FUEL to the front, giving EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means convenient and of practical use, as useful does.

clue.text: Cover over offensive letter in home of midweek team?

indicators.note: over means the cover is laid over and around the letter

parts.note: a shield is a cover or protection
eff is the spelt-out F, euphemism for a swear word

explanation.surface: A rude letter covered over at the base of a team that plays midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Sheffield is home to the football club Sheffield Wednesday, named after a weekday.

clue.text: Where cones are located on street in front of van

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: fir trees bear cones

explanation.surface: Traffic cones set out on a street ahead of a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cones' suggests traffic cones but means pine cones on a tree; 'in front of' joins the definition, 'van' meaning the leading position.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van is to be at the forefront, the leading place.

clue.text: Fighter with five-stone advantage who beat heavyweight?

definitions.text: Fighter with five-stone advantage who beat heavyweight?

parts.words: Fighter with five-stone advantage who beat heavyweight?
parts.note: the biblical youth who took five smooth stones for his sling and slew the giant Goliath

explanation.surface: A boxer who outweighed his opponent by five stone beat a heavyweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five-stone' sounds like a boxing weight gap (a stone is 14 pounds) but means five pebbles.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the shepherd boy armed with a sling and five stones killed the giant Goliath.

clue.text: Doctor or vet to get active constituent

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor or vet becomes an active ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' suggests a component, but means a member of an electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent who takes part in an election by casting a ballot is an active one.

clue.text: Monk in a river, succeeding when he gets fish, in short?

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after the abbreviation

parts.words: when he gets fish, in short
parts.note: Fri, short for Friday, is the day Catholics traditionally eat fish

explanation.surface: A monk out on a river catches fish, as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, akin to a monk.

clue.text: Runs around a little while creating minor nuisances

indicators.note: around means the word for runs wraps the other pieces

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bit is a short while, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: Someone runs about briefly, causing small annoyances.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect bites are small irritations; a fleabite is figuratively any trifling annoyance.

clue.text: In leaderless Britain, left without serious consideration

indicators.note: In means the letter for left sits inside the shortened word
leaderless means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: Blighty is old slang for Britain, from soldiers' use

explanation.surface: With no one in charge, Britain was left without serious thought.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY is soldiers' slang for Britain; 'leaderless' drops its B to give LIGHTY, and L goes 'In' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter lightly is to dismiss it casually, without weighing it seriously.

clue.text: Stuff about English and their once and future king?

indicators.note: about means the word for stuff goes around the letter

parts.note: to gorge is to stuff oneself

explanation.surface: A tale of stuffing the English, and the legendary king who will return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once and future king' recalls Arthur, but means the six past King Georges and Prince George, heir in line; 'their' refers to the English.
explanation.definitionFit: England has had six kings of that name and a prince of it stands in line for the throne.
